cells.requirement: The maximum tenant screening fee a landlord can charge is capped at $68.96 for 2026 (or $30 base adjusted annually). Landlords cannot charge a fee if no unit is available and must provide an itemized receipt, a copy of any obtained credit report, and a refund of unused fees.

Landlords are generally limited to charging a security deposit of up to one month's rent (two months' rent for qualifying small landlords owning two or fewer properties with four or fewer units total). Deposits must be returned within 21 days after the tenant vacates, accompanied by an itemized statement of deductions.

Housing providers are prohibited from discriminating based on protected characteristics including source of income (such as Section 8 vouchers), using blanket criminal bans, or considering arrests without convictions. Landlords must also offer alternative credit evidence options to subsidy recipients and aggregate cohabitant incomes.

Under the Cartwright Act, it is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm to collude on pricing or terms, or to coerce another person to adopt pricing recommendations from such an algorithm.

Landlords may not terminate a residential tenancy without just cause after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months (or 24 months if an adult tenant is added). No-fault evictions require relocation assistance or a final month rent waiver equal to one month's rent.

Landlords are prohibited from increasing the gross rental rate by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, applicable to buildings older than 15 years.
cells.key_value: 5% plus cost of living change or 10% lower limit
